title: A Pentest Waiver That the New Rule Eliminated
scenario_text:
A security-compliance lead at Cedarholm Security must decide whether a penetration-test waiver can be granted before a product launch, given how a comparable waiver was handled last year.

**Decision A (2023-11-14)**
A pentest waiver was granted for an application ahead of launch. Note: 'Under the security policy then in effect, waivers were permitted for applications with limited exposure if a Director signed off. The app in question handled some customer data and the waiver was approved with Director sign-off.'

**Current request C (2024-12-03)**
A product team wants a pentest waiver to hit a launch date for an application that stores and processes customer personally identifiable information (PII). They ask for the waiver 'the same way it was granted last year,' with a Director's sign-off.

**Security Policy (current, updated 2024-07-01, in force now)**
Any application that stores or processes customer PII MUST pass a penetration test before launch. Waivers of the pre-launch pentest are no longer available for PII-handling applications at any approval level. The prior Director-sign-off waiver path was removed for PII-handling systems in the July 2024 update.

**Slack — #appsec**
PM: 'We got a pentest waiver last November with a Director's approval and launched on time. Let's do the same here so we don't slip the date.'
Lead: 'Last November was under the old policy. The waiver path for PII apps was removed in July — a Director's signature can't unlock it now.'

The application handles customer PII, and there is no incident or exception path that changes that.
question: Under the current security policy, what must happen before this PII-handling application can launch? Provide the required step.
